title: Why a rolling ball stops sooner on grass than on ice
examples: Why do things slide on ice?

explain.say: Roll a ball across a football pitch and it soon slows and stops. Roll the same ball on an ice rink and it glides on and on. Why? Look at the ball on the board, rolling to the right, with an arrow pointing back.

draw.text: Why a rolling ball stops sooner on grass than on ice

explain.say: That backwards arrow is friction. Friction is a force that pushes against things that rub or roll over each other. Long grass is bumpy and rough, so it rubs on the ball a lot and slows it quickly. Rub your hands together fast: can you feel friction making them warm?

Now look at the ball on ice. See how tiny the friction arrow is? Ice is very smooth and slippery, so there is hardly any friction to slow the ball. It keeps rolling much further. Have you ever slipped on a wet, shiny floor?

forces.label: Friction from ice
forces.ask: Why do things slide on ice?

explain.say: Look at these bars for the same gentle push. Which surface wins? See Ice light up: the smoother the surface, the further the ball rolls. Long grass is shortest, then carpet, then wooden floor, and ice goes furthest!

But friction is not the bad guy! The friction arrow on grass also helps: it lets your shoes grip so you can walk and run without slipping. Great thinking! Wow fact: without friction, you could not even pick up a pencil, because it would slide right out of your fingers.

faq.a: Friction is a force that acts when two surfaces rub or roll against each other. It always pushes against the movement and slows things down.

faq.q: Why do things slide on ice?
faq.a: Ice is very smooth, and a thin wet layer on top makes it even more slippery, so there is very little friction to slow things down.
Yes! Friction lets shoes grip the ground, lets car brakes stop a car, and lets us hold things. Without it, everything would slip and slide.

faq.q: Why do rough surfaces have more friction?
faq.a: Rough surfaces have bumps that catch and rub against each other, so they push back harder against movement than smooth ones.

faq.q: Why do football boots have studs?
faq.a: Studs dig into the grass and give extra grip, which is extra friction, so players can run and turn quickly without slipping.
asks: Why do shoes have patterns on the bottom?

facts: Friction acts in the opposite direction to motion.
Rubbing your hands together warms them because friction turns movement energy into heat.

quiz.say: Where will a ball roll furthest after the same push?
quiz.why: Ice is the smoothest, so it has the least friction and the ball rolls furthest.

wrong.0: Long grass is rough, with lots of friction.
wrong.1: Carpet has more friction than ice.

quiz.say: Why can you walk without slipping on a dry path?
quiz.show: You can walk on a dry path because…
quiz.why: Friction between your shoes and the path stops your feet sliding.

wrong.2: Air does not push you along when you walk.
